hints.S32_A1: The student wants THE MEANING OF THE UNFAMILIAR WORD and he goes to AN ONLINE DICTIONARY. Ask: which phrasal verb means searching a reference source for a piece of information? 'Delete' and 'print out' never tell you what a word means.
hints.S32_A2: WITHIN MINUTES the news reached the whole COUNTRY after one post on SOCIAL MEDIA. Ask: which verb shows something moving out quickly to many people and places at once? 'Froze' would stop it; 'erased' would remove it.
hints.S32_A3: The clue follows the blank: the engineer is FIXING THE ERRORS IN THE CODE of the FAULTY SOFTWARE. Ask: which verb means hunting down and repairing mistakes inside a program? 'Duplicate' would only copy the same errors.
hints.S32_A4: The work must travel from the students' own devices TO THE CLASS-SHARING DRIVE. Ask: which verb means sending a file from your device onto a shared space online? 'Delete' and 'erase' would destroy the PRESENTATIONS instead.
hints.S32_A5: The sentence praises A KEY SKILL that works ACROSS CULTURES AND LANGUAGES - communication that succeeds. Ask: does the adverb describe a message that achieves its purpose, or one that fails? 'Vaguely' and 'carelessly' describe failure.
hints.S32_B1: EVERY MORNING signals a habit that repeats, and the subject is THE CLASS MONITOR - one person. Ask: in the simple present, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s? 'Wrote' would push the habit into the past.
hints.S32_B2: AFTER TWO YEARS OF TESTING - the work is over, so the moment is finished and past. Ask: which form shows a completed past action? This verb is regular, so the past takes the ordinary ending.
hints.S32_B3: THE INTERNET CONNECTION SUDDENLY DROPPED - one sharp event cutting into something already under way. Ask: which choice shows an action still in progress at that past moment? A plain past verb reports only a finished job.
hints.S32_B4: The statement is positive and set in the past: the app WAS EASY TO USE. Ask: after a positive statement, does the tag turn negative, or stay positive? And must the tag keep the tense the statement gives it?
hints.S32_B5: Look at the statement about THE CHILDREN and their EMAILS: it is a negative one. Ask: after a negative statement, does the tag stay negative or flip to positive? The tag must repeat the statement's own helping verb - 'did' belongs to another tense.
hints.S32_B6: 'A GREAT DEAL OF CONFUSION' counts as one single amount, not many things, and THE WEBSITE CRASHED puts it firmly in the past. Ask: does a singular subject take a present form, or a past one? 'Were' would need a plural.
hints.S32_B7: THE PODCAST cannot make itself - A GROUP OF PRIMARY 5 AND 6 STUDENTS makes it, and they TAKE TURNS EVERY WEEK. Ask: which choice puts the subject on the receiving end, in the present? Passive = a form of 'be' + past participle.
hints.S32_B8: TOLD HIS STUDENTS = a reported command, and this one is negative: PASSWORDS must stay secret, EVEN CLOSE FRIENDS included. Ask: which negative word comes first, and which verb form follows it - plain, -ing, or the infinitive?
hints.S32_C1: WITH THE INTERNET, the ability belongs to us right now, INSTANTLY, all over the world. Ask: which modal shows a present ability? A past-ability modal would suit the sentence about the days before smartphones, not this one.
hints.S32_C2: The passage is giving advice: we ALWAYS CHECK whether information is ACCURATE BEFORE WE SHARE IT. Ask: which modal tells you the right and responsible thing to do? A modal of pure possibility would make the advice sound optional.
hints.S32_C3: This sentence states A RULE: pupils use the laboratory ONLY WHEN A TEACHER IS PRESENT, and NOBODY IS ALLOWED to break it. Ask: which modal gives permission? 'Might' would only guess at a possibility, which no rule does.
hints.S32_C4: A message THAT SEEMS HARMLESS could still upset someone IF IT IS MISUNDERSTOOD - the harm is possible, never certain. Ask: which modal shows the weaker possibility? 'Will' would promise that the upset happens every single time.
hints.S32_C5: IN THE FUTURE, technology makes communication EVEN FASTER AND MORE RELIABLE - this is what we expect to happen. Ask: which modal marks a plain future expectation? 'Would' belongs to an imagined situation, not a real one.
hints.S32_C6: WITHOUT THEIR PHONES is an imagined situation - these people are not actually without them. Ask: which modal shows the result of a situation that is only supposed, not real? A plain future modal belongs to things that really happen.
hints.S32_C7: BEFORE SMARTPHONES EXISTED - the ability described is over and done with, and it was limited: BY LETTER OR TELEPHONE only. Ask: which modal shows a past ability? The present-ability modal is needed by blank 1.
hints.S32_C8: The blank opens a QUESTION, and the sentence proposes something: BRING PEOPLE TOGETHER rather than DRIVE THEM APART. Ask: which modal begins a suggestion made with 'we'? It is not the advice modal from blank 2.
hints.S32_D1: IN THE PAST only LARGE ORGANISATIONS could reach MILLIONS OF PEOPLE AT ONCE - think of a radio or television station. Ask: which box word means sending news out widely to a huge audience? The blank follows 'could', so it must be a plain verb.
hints.S32_D2: The dash tells you the job: SEPARATING FACTS FROM OPINIONS and CHECKING SOURCES before you believe anything. Ask: which box word means sifting information and keeping only what is trustworthy? It follows 'to', so it must be a plain verb.
hints.S32_D3: The clue sits right after the blank: THEIR REAL NAMES ARE HIDDEN, so nobody can be held RESPONSIBLE. Ask: which box word describes an account with no name attached to it? It must be a describing word, since 'accounts' follows.
hints.S32_D4: Knowledge now reaches PEOPLE EVERYWHERE - EVEN IN REMOTE AREAS. Ask: which box word means easy for anyone to reach or obtain? The blank follows 'has made knowledge', so it must describe knowledge, not a machine.
hints.S32_D5: Scientists send RESEARCH FINDINGS TO COLLEAGUES ACROSS THE GLOBE IN SECONDS. Ask: which box word means passing information electronically from one place to another? The blank follows 'can', so a noun cannot go here.
hints.S32_E1: The underlined word tells us HOW the teacher EXPLAINED - and explaining is an action. Ask: does an action take an adjective, or an adverb? Adverbs of manner nearly always gain the same two-letter tail.
hints.S32_E2: GROWN MEN AND WOMANS: this noun does not take a plain -s. Ask: what happens to 'man' when there is more than one? Apply exactly the same vowel change here.
hints.S32_E3: Count the consonants at the end of 'CONNECT': there are two of them. Ask: do we double a final consonant when another consonant already stands in front of it? Doubling follows only a short vowel plus ONE consonant.
hints.S32_E4: THE MESSAGES is plural - more than one message went astray. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Never let 'the wrong email address' sitting nearby decide the verb for you.
hints.S32_E5: The POSTERS belong to the CHILDRENS - and that spelling is wrong twice over. Ask: is 'children' already a plural on its own? So where must the apostrophe go, and does the extra -s stay or vanish?
hints.S32_F1: The teacher's exact words were spoken to THE CLASS, and inside the speech marks they are called 'YOU'. Ask: when you report those words to somebody else, which pronoun takes over from 'you'? The speech marks disappear with it.
hints.S32_F2: The given sentence is passive: THE SCHOOL'S NEW WEBSITE receives the action, and A TEAM OF STUDENT VOLUNTEERS does it. Ask: when the doer moves to the front, what happens to 'was' and to the word 'by'? The verb becomes a plain past form.
